identificationModule.briefTitle: Aquatic Power Training Dosing Strategies and Creatine Supplementation in Older Adults
identificationModule.officialTitle: Optimization of Aquatic Power Training Dosing Strategies and the Effects of Creatine Supplementation on Functional and Multisystem Adaptations in Older Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial

descriptionModule.briefSummary:
This randomized controlled trial will investigate the effects of different aquatic power training dosing strategies and creatine supplementation on functional and multisystem adaptations in community-dwelling older adults.

Participants will be randomly allocated to one of five parallel groups: (1) aquatic power training regulated according to rating of perceived exertion during the first repetition (RPE-1) plus placebo; (2) aquatic power training using a conventional time-based dosing strategy plus placebo; (3) time-based aquatic power training plus creatine supplementation; (4) sedentary control plus placebo; or (5) sedentary control plus creatine supplementation.

The intervention will last 16 weeks. Aquatic training will be performed three times per week for approximately 60 minutes per session. Participants allocated to creatine supplementation will receive 3 g/day of creatine monohydrate, whereas the corresponding placebo groups will receive a visually indistinguishable placebo following the same supplementation schedule.

The primary outcomes will assess body composition, muscle strength, and functional capacity. Additional outcomes will examine bone health, cardiometabolic health, inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers, immune function, neurobiological and cognitive function, quality of life, sleep quality, psychological status, fatigue, and affective state.

Assessments will be performed before and after the 16-week intervention.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription:
Participants will be randomly allocated to one of five parallel groups and will complete a 16-week intervention period. The study is designed to evaluate two complementary research questions: (1) whether an aquatic power training program regulated using rating of perceived exertion during the first repetition (RPE-1) produces different adaptations compared with a conventional time-based aquatic power training strategy; and (2) whether daily creatine supplementation enhances the adaptations associated with aquatic power training and/or modifies outcomes in sedentary older adults.

\*\*Aquatic Power Training\*\*

Participants allocated to either aquatic training condition will complete a 16-week supervised aquatic power training program consisting of three sessions per week, with each session lasting approximately 60 minutes.

The exercise program will focus on the development of muscular power using aquatic exercise. The two training conditions will follow the same overall intervention period and training frequency but will differ in the strategy used to regulate exercise dosage.

In the \*\*RPE-1 aquatic power training condition\*\*, exercise dosage will be regulated according to the participant's rating of perceived exertion during the first repetition (RPE-1). This strategy will be used to individualize and regulate the exercise stimulus during the training program.

In the \*\*time-based aquatic power training condition\*\*, exercise dosage will be prescribed using a conventional time-based strategy. Participants will therefore perform the aquatic power training according to the predefined temporal prescription rather than using RPE-1 to regulate exercise dosage.

Aquatic training sessions will be conducted under supervision at the Piscina Cubierta de Benimàmet (Fundación Deportiva Municipal, Valencia, Spain).

\*\*Creatine and Placebo Supplementation\*\*

Participants assigned to creatine supplementation will receive \*\*3 g/day of creatine monohydrate\*\* throughout the 16-week intervention. Supplementation will be taken daily, including non-training days, and no loading phase will be used.

Participants assigned to placebo supplementation will receive a visually indistinguishable placebo following the same daily supplementation schedule.

Creatine and placebo supplementation will be administered under double-blind conditions. Neither participants nor investigators responsible for supplementation administration will know the supplementation allocation until completion of the study.

\*\*Study Groups\*\*

Participants will be randomly allocated to one of the following five groups:

1. \*\*RPE-1 Aquatic Power Training + Placebo:\*\* 16 weeks of aquatic power training, three sessions per week, with exercise dosage regulated according to RPE-1, combined with daily placebo supplementation.
2. \*\*Time-Based Aquatic Power Training + Placebo:\*\* 16 weeks of aquatic power training, three sessions per week, using a conventional time-based dosing strategy, combined with daily placebo supplementation.
3. \*\*Time-Based Aquatic Power Training + Creatine:\*\* 16 weeks of aquatic power training, three sessions per week, using the conventional time-based dosing strategy, combined with 3 g/day of creatine monohydrate.
4. \*\*Sedentary Control + Placebo:\*\* Participants will not participate in the aquatic power training intervention and will receive placebo supplementation daily throughout the 16-week study period.
5. \*\*Sedentary Control + Creatine:\*\* Participants will not participate in the aquatic power training intervention and will receive 3 g/day of creatine monohydrate throughout the 16-week study period.

Participants allocated to the sedentary control conditions will be instructed to maintain their usual lifestyle during the intervention period and not to initiate a structured moderate- or high-intensity strength or power training program.

\*\*Assessment Schedule\*\*

Outcome assessments will be performed before the intervention and immediately after completion of the 16-week intervention. Assessments will include body composition, muscle strength, functional capacity, bone metabolism, cardiometabolic health, inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers, immune function, neurobiological and cognitive function, quality of life, sleep quality, psychological status, fatigue, affective state, and clinical safety measures.

Questionnaires and cognitive assessments will be administered in person and distributed across two assessment sessions at each evaluation period to reduce participant fatigue.

Because of the nature of the exercise intervention, participants and personnel supervising the training cannot be blinded to the aquatic power training dosing strategy. However, outcome assessors and investigators responsible for statistical analyses will remain blinded to group allocation.

interventions.name: RPE-1 Aquatic Power Training-Placebo
interventions.description:
Participants will complete a 16-week supervised aquatic power training program, consisting of three sessions per week, with each session lasting approximately 60 minutes. Exercises will be performed at maximal intended movement velocity.

For each exercise, participants will perform 4 sets of 8 repetitions. Exercise intensity will be regulated using ratings of perceived exertion (RPE) obtained during the set. During the first repetition (RPE-1), the target RPE will be 4 for the active muscles or 3 for the overall body. By the last repetition of the set, the target RPE will be 6 for the active muscles or 5 for the overall body.

Participants will perform active recovery for 120 seconds between sets and 90 seconds between exercises.

This RPE-based dosing strategy will be used to individualize the aquatic power training stimulus according to each participant's perceived exertion while maintaining maximal intended movement velocity.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Change in Body Composition via Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA)
primaryOutcomes.description: Whole body and segmental composition will be assessed through Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA). Parameters analyzed will be: total and regional fat mass and lean mass and % of fat mass.
Handgrip strength (Kg) will be assessed using hand-held dynamometry. Higher values indicate greater muscle strength

primaryOutcomes.measure: Change in lower limb Isokinetic muscle strength
primaryOutcomes.description: knee flexo-extension muscle strength will be assessed using an isokinetic dynamometer (Biodex®) at an angular velocity of 180°/s. Peak torque will be recorded in Newton-meters (Nm), with higher values indicating greater strength

primaryOutcomes.measure: Change in upper limb Isokinetic muscle Strength
primaryOutcomes.description: Elbow flexo-extension muscle strength will be assessed using an isokinetic dynamometer (Biodex®) at an angular velocity of 180°/s. Peak torque will be recorded in Newton-meters (Nm), with higher values indicating greater strength

primaryOutcomes.measure: Change in functional mobility and agility performance
primaryOutcomes.description: Functional mobility and agility will be assessed using the Timed Up and Go Test. The time required to stand from a chair, walk the standardized distance, turn, return, and sit down will be recorded in seconds. Lower values indicate better functional performance.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Change in lower body functional performance
primaryOutcomes.description: Lower-body functional capacity (resistance strength) will be assessed using the 30-Second Chair Stand Test. The number of complete sit-to-stand repetitions performed within 30 seconds will be recorded. Higher values indicate better functional performance.
Functional aerobic capacity will be assessed using the 6-Minute Walk Test. The total distance walked during six minutes will be recorded in meters. Higher values indicate better functional capacity.

secondaryOutcomes.description: Serum procollagen type I N-terminal propeptide (P1NP) will be measured as a marker of bone formation.
Serum C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen (β-CTX) will be measured as a marker of bone resorption

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change in cardiometabolic health (systolic blood pressure)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Resting systolic blood pressure will be assessed and expressed in millimeters of mercury (mmHg), with lower values generally indicating lower cardiovascular risk.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change in cardiometabolic health (diastolic blood pressure)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Resting diastolic blood pressure will be assessed and expressed in millimeters of mercury (mmHg), with lower values generally indicating lower cardiovascular risk.
Total cholesterol levels will be collected through a blood sample in the morning in a fasted state to assess metabolic state.
HDL cholesterol levels will be collected through a blood sample in the morning in a fasted state to assess metabolic state.
LDL cholesterol levels will be collected through a blood sample in the morning in a fasted state to assess metabolic state.
Triglycerides levels will be collected through a blood sample in the morning in a fasted state to assess metabolic state.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change in metabolic biomarkers (fasting plasma glucose)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Fasting plasma glucose concentration will be measured from blood samples collected after an overnight fasting period to assess changes in glucose homeostasis and metabolic state
Circulating glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) concentration will be measured from blood samples to assess changes in this gut-derived metabolic hormone involved in glucose regulation
Circulating interleukin-6 (IL-6) concentration will be measured from blood samples as a biomarker of systemic low-grade inflammation.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change in inflammation biomarkers (Tumor Necrosis Factor-Alpha Concentration)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Circulating tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) will be measured from blood samples as a biomarker of systemic low-grade inflammation.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change in Oxidative stress biomarkers (F2-Isoprostane Concentration)
secondaryOutcomes.description: F2-isoprostanes will be measured from blood samples as biomarkers of oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change in Oxidative stress biomarkers (Glutathione Peroxidase Activity)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Glutathione peroxidase (GPx) activity will be measured from blood samples as a marker of antioxidant defense.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change in Immune system (Total Leukocyte Count)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Total circulating leukocyte count will be measured from peripheral blood samples to assess changes in overall immune cell status
Circulating neutrophil count will be measured from peripheral blood samples to assess changes in the neutrophil component of the immune response
Circulating lymphocyte count will be measured from peripheral blood samples to assess changes in the lymphocyte component of immune function
Circulating monocyte count will be measured from peripheral blood samples to assess changes in this component of the innate immune system
Circulating eosinophil count will be measured from peripheral blood samples to assess changes in this leukocyte population
Circulating basophil count will be measured from peripheral blood samples to assess changes in this leukocyte population
Circulating platelet count will be measured from peripheral blood samples to assess changes in platelet levels

The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) will be calculated by dividing the absolute neutrophil count by the absolute lymphocyte count. NLR will be used as an integrated hematological marker of systemic inflammatory and immune status.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change in Immune system (Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index )
secondaryOutcomes.description: The Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) will be calculated from peripheral blood platelet, neutrophil, and lymphocyte counts as an integrated marker of systemic immune-inflammatory status.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change in Neurobiological function (Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor concentration)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Circulating brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) concentration will be measured from blood samples to assess changes in a neurotrophic factor involved in neuronal function and neuroplasticity .

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change in Cognitive function (Trail Making Test Part A Completion Time)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Cognitive performance will be assessed using the Trail Making Test Part A (TMT-A), which primarily evaluates visual attention, processing speed, and visuomotor tracking. Participants will be instructed to connect numbered targets sequentially as quickly and accurately as possible. Completion time will be recorded in seconds, with lower completion times indicating better performance.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Change in Cognitive function (Trail Making Test Part B Completion Time)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Executive and attentional performance will be assessed using the Trail Making Test Part B (TMT-B), which requires participants to alternate sequentially between numbered and lettered targets. The test primarily assesses cognitive flexibility, set-shifting, divided attention, and executive function. Completion time will be recorded in seconds, with lower completion times indicating better performance.

otherOutcomes.description: Quality of life in older adults will be assessed using the World Health Organization Quality of Life-OLD (WHOQOL-OLD) questionnaire, which evaluates relevant dimensions of quality of life specifically related to older populations. Changes in questionnaire scores will be used to assess the effect on perceived quality of life.

otherOutcomes.measure: Change in Health-Related Quality of Life Assessed by the EQ-5D-5L
otherOutcomes.description: Health-related quality of life will be assessed using the EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level (EQ-5D-5L) questionnaire. The instrument evaluates health status across five dimensions: mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression. Changes in EQ-5D-5L health status will be used to assess the effect on perceived health-related quality of life.

otherOutcomes.measure: Change in Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index Score
otherOutcomes.description: Sleep quality will be assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), which evaluates different aspects of sleep over the preceding month. Changes in the global PSQI score will be used to assess sleep quality, with higher scores indicating poorer sleep quality

Depressive symptoms will be assessed using the 9-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9). Changes in the total score will be used to assess depressive symptom severity, with higher scores indicating greater severity of depressive symptoms.

Fatigue will be assessed using the 10-item Fatigue Assessment Scale (FAS). Each item is rated on a five-point response scale ranging from 1 (never) to 5 (always). Changes in the total FAS score will be used to assess perceived fatigue, with higher scores indicating greater fatigue.

Positive affect will be assessed using the Positive Affect subscale of the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS). The PANAS comprises 20 affect-related items rated on a five-point response scale. Changes in the Positive Affect subscale score will be used to assess changes in positive emotional state, with higher scores indicating greater positive affect.
Serum creatinine concentration will be assessed as a clinical safety marker related to renal function.
Serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) concentration will be assessed as a clinical safety marker related to liver function.
Serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST) concentration will be assessed as a clinical safety marker related to liver function.
Adverse events potentially associated with the aquatic exercise intervention or creatine/placebo supplementation will be recorded and clinically evaluated throughout the intervention period.

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age ≥60 years at enrollment.
2. Community-dwelling and functionally independent in basic activities of daily living.
3. Able to ambulate independently, with or without usual assistive devices, and able to safely perform the physical assessments included in the study.
4. Clinically stable; participants with chronic diseases must have maintained stable pharmacological treatment for at least three months before the intervention.
5. Not currently participating in a structured moderate- or high-intensity strength or power training program or another systematic supervised exercise program.
6. Available and willing to participate throughout the 16-week intervention and complete all scheduled assessments.
7. Willing to accept random allocation to any study group and creatine or placebo supplementation when applicable.
8. Willing to maintain stable dietary habits throughout the intervention.
9. Able and willing to provide written informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Uncontrolled cardiovascular, respiratory, metabolic, neurological, or musculoskeletal disease contraindicating exercise or limiting safe participation.
2. Unfavorable medical assessment for participation in supervised exercise.
3. Uncontrolled hypertension at screening.
4. Known kidney disease, renal failure, or clinically relevant impairment of renal function.
5. Active liver disease or clinically relevant impairment of liver function.
6. Active malignant neoplasm or current cancer treatment.
7. Endocrine or metabolic disorders considered by the research team to substantially interfere with the study's primary outcomes.
8. Current use, or use during the previous three months, of creatine or other supplements with potential ergogenic or anabolic effects.
9. Pharmacological treatment considered likely to substantially modify the study's primary outcomes.
10. Participation during the previous three months in a systematic moderate- or high-intensity strength or power training program.

identificationModule.briefTitle: Effects of Chronic Creatine and Beta-Hydroxy-Beta-Methylbutyrate Supplementation on Oxidative Stress, Inflammation, Muscle Strength, and Body Composition in Individuals With Down Syndrome
identificationModule.officialTitle: Effects of Chronic Creatine and Beta-Hydroxy-Beta-Methylbutyrate Supplementation on Oxidative Stress, Inflammation, Muscle Strength, and Body Composition in Individuals With Down Syndrome

descriptionModule.briefSummary:
Purpose:

This study will test whether 8 weeks of creatine and HMB supplementation can improve muscle strength, body composition, balance, and overall health in people with Down syndrome. Participants will also receive nutrition tips during the study.

Who can participate:

People with Down syndrome who can perform basic physical tasks. Must provide consent from the participant and legal guardian.

What participants will do:

Take creatine (3 g/day) and HMB (3 g/day) or placebo for 8 weeks. Complete tests for muscle strength, balance, and cognitive function. Undergo body composition scans and give blood samples for health markers.

Timing:

All tests and blood samples are taken before and after each 8-week period.

Importance:

Results will help determine if creatine and HMB can safely improve strength, balance, and overall health in people with Down syndrome.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription:
This study is an 8-week randomized, placebo-controlled, crossover trial designed to evaluate the effects of daily supplementation with creatine monohydrate (3 g) and beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB, 3 g) on body composition, muscle strength, balance, cognitive function, and biomarkers of oxidative stress and inflammation in individuals with Down syndrome. Participants will receive nutritional education throughout the intervention to support a balanced diet.

Primary outcomes include lean mass measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA).

Secondary outcomes include fat-free mass (bioimpedance), bone mineral density (DXA), handgrip strength, lower limb strength (Five Times Sit-to-Stand Test), upper and lower body isometric strength (K-Pull test), balance (4-Stage Balance Test), and cognitive function assessed by the Timed Up and Go Dual Task. Blood biomarkers of oxidative stress and inflammation, including reduced glutathione (GSH), superoxide dismutase (SOD), C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukins (IL-1, IL-6, IL-7), and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), will be assessed before and after each supplementation period.

All assessments will be performed at baseline and at the end of each 8-week supplementation phase, allowing for evaluation of both physiological and functional responses to creatine and HMB supplementation in this population.

secondaryOutcomes.description:
Balance will be using the 4-Stage Balance Test. It involves holding four progressively difficult positions for at least 10 seconds each:

Feet together: 1 point if the position is held for 10 seconds or more. Partial semi-tandem: 1 point if the position is held for 10 seconds or more.

Semi-tandem:

* 2 points: If the position is held for more than 10 seconds.
* 1 point: If the position is held for between 3 and 9.99 seconds.
* 0 points: If the position is held for less than 3 seconds. The score ranges from 0 to 4 (best balance).
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline (within 2 days before starting supplementation) and at 8 weeks (end of supplementation)

secondaryOutcomes.description:
Cognitive function will be assessed with Timed Up and Go Dual Task (TUGdt) test.

The participant first performs the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test alone, standing up from a chair, walking a short distance (3 meters) turning, and sitting back down, while simultaneously naming animals within a 10-second period, which assesses verbal fluency.

The time taken to complete these distances will be recorded, and the fluency in naming the animals will be assessed.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline (within 2 days before starting supplementation) and at 8 weeks (end of supplementation)

secondaryOutcomes.description:
The K-Pull test will be used to evaluate isometric lower body strength

Participants will perform a seated knee extension test, pushing their leg against the dynamometer with maximal effort. Participants will exert their maximum force against the unyielding device for 3-5 seconds. The peak force achieved (in Newtons) over a minimum of two trials will be recorded
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline (within 2 days before starting supplementation) and at 8 weeks (end of supplementation)

secondaryOutcomes.description:
The K-Pull test will be used to evaluate isometric upper body strength

Participants will stand with their back against a wall to stabilize the torso. The participant will be instructed to exert a maximal force by pushing their arm outward against the device for 3-5 seconds.The peak force achieved (in Newtons or kilograms-force) over a minimum of two trials will be recorded.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Baseline (within 2 days before starting supplementation) and at 8 weeks (end of supplementation)

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis: Medical confirmation of Down syndrome (trisomy of chromosome 21).
* Physical capacity: Ability to perform basic physical tests (e.g., standing up from a chair or walking without assistance).
* Informed consent: Informed consent will be obtained from both the participant and their legal representative, in compliance with current legislation for individuals requiring support measures.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Chronic kidney disease: Diagnosis of chronic kidney disease.
* Severe motor limitations: Inability to perform the required physical tests (e.g., paralysis or mobility impairments preventing the execution of muscle strength assessments).
* Participation in other studies: Participation in another nutritional or supplementation intervention study within the last 6 months.
* Allergies or intolerances: Known allergy to creatine or to components of the placebo (inulin).
